facts.text: Scituate’s harbor has long been a maritime hub, with the historic Minot’s Ledge Lighthouse nicknamed the “I Love You Lighthouse” for its 1–4–3 flashing pattern.
In 2002, residents passed the Community Preservation Act, buying over 400 acres of open space, restoring Lawson Tower, and protecting the Mordecai Lincoln Homestead.
Scituate once hosted the shortwave radio station WNYW, broadcasting internationally in the late 1960s.
The North Scituate station sits beside historic shops and restaurants, making it a convenient stop for travelers exploring the town’s heritage.
The Scituate Historical Society, founded in 1917, preserves more than 300 years of local history through museums, trails, and annual harbor events.
